meta.title: The Pill That Works Before It Dissolves
meta.theme: why placebo effects are largest for pain, and what makes them larger still

format.format_verified: 2026-09: five sentences, TITA, +3 with no negative marking, consistent in released papers 2016 to 2025; re-verify against each new official paper

traps.description: Camouflage: the outlier is about placebos in clinical trials, shares the paragraph's key noun and even opens with 'therefore', so a topic matcher and a connective matcher both keep it. It does not explain why the effect varies, which is the core's only business.

meta.learning_objective: tell a sentence that uses the paragraph's subject for a different purpose (method) from the sentences that explain a finding

quality.adversarial_review: The strongest wrong answer is D, the sentence about injections and doctors: it is the only one that reads like a list of findings rather than an explanation, and a reader who wants the paragraph to be 'about the brain' may drop it. It stays because its 'also' extends C's statement about the size of the effect, and because the core would otherwise end on a single example. E survives a topic check and a connective check and fails only the purpose check: nothing in A–D concerns how trials are designed, and nothing after E would use the point.

source.usage_note: Original composition in CAT register for CAT OS. General account of placebo analgesia; no specific text adapted. Personal study only.

meta.prompt_version: content engine v1 (content/taxonomy/AUTHORING.md); the v2 exemplar
meta.reviewer_notes: A medium-tier item where the outlier shares the noun, the field and a connective with the core. The item teaches that 'therefore' is not a passport: a sentence must serve the paragraph's purpose, not merely follow from its topic.

sentences.label: A
sentences.text: Pain is not a simple readout of tissue damage; it is a judgement the brain makes about threat, using every source of information it has.

sentences.label: B
sentences.text: A pill the patient believes in is one such source, and it can shift the judgement before any chemistry is involved.

sentences.label: C
sentences.text: This is why placebo effects are largest for pain and smallest for conditions the brain does not construct in the same way, such as infections.

sentences.label: D
sentences.text: The size of the effect also grows with the ritual around the pill: an injection outperforms a tablet, and a tablet from a doctor outperforms one from a nurse.

sentences.label: E
sentences.text: Clinical trials therefore compare a new drug against a placebo, so that only the chemistry is being measured.

builder.prompt: Build the four-sentence explanation of why a placebo works best on pain. Start from what pain is, and let each sentence hand something to the next. The sentence with no seat is your answer.

explanation.spine_note: The core explains one finding in four steps. A redefines pain as a judgement the brain makes from evidence. B makes a believed-in pill one piece of that evidence. C draws the consequence: placebos work best where the brain constructs the experience, so pain most and infections least. D adds a second factor in the size of the effect, the ritual. Define, apply, conclude, extend.

core_roles.label: A
core_roles.why_here: It sets the frame everything else uses, pain as a judgement from information, and needs nothing before it.

core_roles.label: B
core_roles.why_here: 'One such source' picks up A's 'every source of information' and places the pill inside the frame.

core_roles.label: C
core_roles.why_here: 'This is why' draws the consequence of A and B together: the effect is largest where the brain does the constructing.

core_roles.label: D
core_roles.why_here: 'Also' extends C's statement about the size of the effect with a second factor, the ritual, and closes the account.

links.explanation: B's 'one such source' substitutes for A's 'every source of information it has'; the phrase cannot be read without A.
C's 'This is why' takes the mechanism of A and B as its cause and states the effect it explains.
D's 'the effect' and 'also' continue C's subject, the size of the placebo effect, and add to it.

explanation.violation_named: E is about the same thing and does a different job. The four core sentences explain why the placebo effect is large for pain and what makes it larger; E describes how clinical trials are designed. It is a statement of method in a paragraph of findings, and no sentence in the core prepares for it or follows from it.
explanation.why_it_breaks: E's 'therefore' promises a consequence of what came before, but nothing in A–D concerns trial design, so the connective has nothing to draw on; and E's point, measure only the chemistry, runs against the paragraph's interest, which is precisely the part that is not chemistry. Insert E anywhere and the paragraph changes subject for one sentence and changes back.
explanation.trap_exposed: The camouflage is double. E shares the noun 'placebo' with every core sentence, and it opens with 'therefore', which a fast reader treats as proof of belonging. Neither test is the right one. Belonging is about purpose: the core explains an effect, and E uses the effect to say something about method.

exclusion_analysis.label: A
exclusion_analysis.why_tempting: It is the only sentence that never mentions a pill or a placebo, and it reads like a definition from a different, more general essay.
exclusion_analysis.what_breaks: Without A, B's 'one such source' has nothing to be a source of, and C's 'the brain does not construct in the same way' loses the frame it depends on.

exclusion_analysis.label: B
exclusion_analysis.why_tempting: It is short and transitional, and a reader who has not seen the substitution in 'one such source' may find no obvious slot for it.
exclusion_analysis.what_breaks: Without B, C's 'This is why' has no mechanism to draw on: nothing has yet connected belief to the brain's judgement.

exclusion_analysis.label: C
exclusion_analysis.why_tempting: 'This is why' makes C look like a conclusion, and a reader may treat it as an ending that D then contradicts by continuing.
exclusion_analysis.what_breaks: Without C the paragraph never states the finding it exists to explain, and D's 'the effect' and 'also' refer to a size that has not been mentioned.

exclusion_analysis.label: D
exclusion_analysis.why_tempting: It is a list of concrete comparisons, injection, tablet, doctor, nurse, where the rest of the core is explanatory, so its register feels different.
exclusion_analysis.what_breaks: Without D the account ends on C's single contrast and never extends it; and D's 'also' shows it was written to follow a sentence about the size of the effect, which only C is.

explanation.detection_habit: Ask what the paragraph is FOR before asking what it is about. Four sentences here explain why an effect varies; one uses the effect to talk about something else. A shared noun and a confident 'therefore' are the two cheapest disguises a stray sentence can wear.

mentor.challenge: Every sentence here mentions the placebo, and one of them even begins with 'therefore'. Build the explanation, and see which sentence explains nothing.
mentor.takeaway: Topic gets a sentence into the room. Purpose gets it a seat.
